```
         TAKE(SORTBY(HSTACK(d, cost, share), cost, -1), 5))
)
```

## Formula 2: department by month matrix
```
=LET(
  d,     SORT(UNIQUE(Costs[Department])),
  mEnd,  TRANSPOSE(SORT(UNIQUE(DATE(YEAR(Costs[Date]), MONTH(Costs[Date]) + 1, 0)))),
  mPrev, DATE(YEAR(mEnd), MONTH(mEnd), 0),
  body,  SUMIFS(Costs[CostUSD], Costs[Department], d,
                Costs[Date], ">" & mPrev, Costs[Date], "<" & (mEnd + 1)),
  VSTACK(HSTACK("Department", mEnd), HSTACK(d, body))
)
```

DATE(year, month+1, 0) returns the last day of the month and works on arrays, which avoids the limitation that EOMONTH does not accept ranges directly. SUMIFS with a column of departments and a row of month boundaries returns a two-dimensional result, so the matrix is produced by a single call. Format the header row as mmm yyyy and the body as currency.

## How to adapt
- Add a total column: wrap with HSTACK(body, BYROW(body, LAMBDA(r, SUM(r)))).
- Rank by growth: subtract the second to last column of body from the last one (INDEX(body,,COLUMNS(body)) minus INDEX(body,,COLUMNS(body)-1)) and sort by the difference.
- Another dimension: replace Department with SubscriptionName, ResourceGroup or a tag column.
- Only one year: add Costs[Date], ">="&DATE(2026,1,1) to the SUMIFS pairs and filter the month list accordingly.

## Required permissions
None in Excel. To export costs you need Cost Management Reader (or higher) on the subscription or billing scope, plus the export or download permission of your portal. Do not paste billing account identifiers into shared workbooks. TAKE, VSTACK, HSTACK and the BYROW variant need a current Microsoft 365 build.

## Common mistakes
- Dates stored as text: SUMIFS compares numbers and returns 0.
- Using EOMONTH on a range: it returns #VALUE!; use the DATE trick or add +0.
- Mixing currencies in one column: convert first.
- Leaving blank tags in: the blank group appears as an empty first row and distorts the ranking.

## Performance and scaling notes
SUMIFS over an Excel table is efficient up to hundreds of thousands of rows, but the matrix formula evaluates departments times months times rows. For very large exports, pre-aggregate by day and department in Power Query (Group By) and point the formulas at the smaller table.

title: Explode semicolon-separated group memberships into a long table with TEXTSPLIT and REDUCE
summary: Convert a column that lists groups per user into one row per user and group, then count members per group, using REDUCE, TEXTSPLIT and VSTACK.
body:
## What it does
Exports often contain one cell such as Sales-EU;Finance;All-Staff per user. That layout is impossible to count or filter. The formulas turn it into a tidy two-column list (user, group) and then summarise how many users each group has.

## Sample data layout
Table Users:

| UserPrincipalName | Groups |
| anna@contoso.example | Sales-EU;Finance;All-Staff |
| ben@contoso.example | All-Staff |
| cho@contoso.example | (blank) |

## Formula 1: long format
```
=LET(
  n, ROWS(Users),
  raw, DROP(
    REDUCE("", SEQUENCE(n),
      LAMBDA(acc, i,
        LET(
          g, TRIM(TOCOL(TEXTSPLIT(INDEX(Users[Groups], i) & "", ";"))),
          VSTACK(acc, HSTACK(IF(g = g, INDEX(Users[UserPrincipalName], i), ""), g))
        )
      )
    ), 1),
  FILTER(raw, INDEX(raw, , 2) <> "", "No memberships")
)
```

How it works: for every row index i, TEXTSPLIT cuts the cell at the semicolons, TOCOL turns the result into a column, and TRIM cleans each group name. IF(g = g, upn, "") repeats the user name for each group so the two columns have equal height. VSTACK appends the block to the accumulator, DROP removes the dummy first row, and FILTER removes blank group names (users without groups). Concatenating & "" turns an empty cell into an empty string so TEXTSPLIT does not receive a zero.

## Formula 2: members per group
Assuming Formula 1 is in cell F2 and spills:
```
=LET(
  grp, INDEX(F2#, , 2),
  g,   SORT(UNIQUE(grp)),
  n,   MAP(g, LAMBDA(x, SUM(--(grp = x)))),
  VSTACK({"Group","Members"}, SORTBY(HSTACK(g, n), n, -1))
)
```

## How to adapt
- Different delimiter: change ";" in TEXTSPLIT, or pass an array of delimiters such as {";",","}.
- Pivot instead of formulas: copy Formula 1 as values and insert a PivotTable counting Group by UserPrincipalName.
- Group names containing the delimiter must be quoted in the export; fix at source or use Power Query's Split Column by Delimiter with quote handling.

## Required permissions
None in Excel. The group lists come from an export; if you generate it with Microsoft Graph, the account needs GroupMember.Read.All or User.Read.All with Group.Read.All and a role such as Directory Readers. TEXTSPLIT, TOCOL, DROP and VSTACK need a current Microsoft 365 build.

## Common mistakes
- Forgetting to wrap TEXTSPLIT output in TOCOL: a row-shaped array would not stack correctly.
- Leading spaces after semicolons produce duplicate group names that look identical; TRIM prevents this.
- Referencing the spill range with a typed range instead of the # operator: new rows would be ignored.

## Performance and scaling notes
REDUCE with VSTACK copies the accumulator on every step, so runtime grows roughly with the square of the row count. It is comfortable for a few thousand users. For tens of thousands, use Power Query: select the Groups column, Split Column > By Delimiter > Advanced > Split into Rows, and load the result; it is faster and uses less memory.

title: Power Query M: combine a folder of CSV exports and keep the source file name
summary: A Power Query M script that appends all CSV files in a folder, tags each row with its file name, applies types and removes duplicates.
body:
## What it does
When an admin portal or script produces one CSV per day or per tenant, you want a single table that grows when you drop in a new file. This Power Query M script reads every CSV in a folder, promotes headers, keeps the file name as a column for traceability, converts types with an explicit culture, and removes duplicate rows.

## Sample data layout
Folder C:\Exports\SignIns contains files such as signins-2026-11-18.csv and signins-2026-11-19.csv. Each file has the columns:

| UserPrincipalName | CreatedDateTime | AppDisplayName | IPAddress | StatusCode |
| anna@contoso.example | 2026-11-19T08:12:00Z | Microsoft Teams | 203.0.113.10 | 0 |

## The M script
Data > Get Data > From Other Sources > Blank Query > Advanced Editor, paste:

```
let
  FolderPath = "C:\Exports\SignIns",
  Files   = Folder.Files(FolderPath),
  CsvOnly = Table.SelectRows(Files, each Text.Lower([Extension]) = ".csv" and not Text.StartsWith([Name], "~")),
  Parsed  = Table.AddColumn(CsvOnly, "Data", each
              Table.PromoteHeaders(
                Csv.Document([Content], [Delimiter = ",", Encoding = 65001, QuoteStyle = QuoteStyle.Csv]),
                [PromoteAllScalars = true])),
  Slim    = Table.SelectColumns(Parsed, {"Name", "Data"}),
  Cols    = List.Distinct(List.Combine(List.Transform(Slim[Data], each Table.ColumnNames(_)))),
  Expanded = Table.ExpandTableColumn(Slim, "Data", Cols, Cols),
  Renamed = Table.RenameColumns(Expanded, {{"Name", "SourceFile"}}),
  Typed   = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Renamed, {
              {"CreatedDateTime", type datetimezone},
              {"StatusCode", Int64.Type},
              {"UserPrincipalName", type text},
              {"AppDisplayName", type text},
              {"IPAddress", type text}}, "en-US"),
  Distinct = Table.Distinct(Typed, {"UserPrincipalName", "CreatedDateTime", "AppDisplayName"})
in
  Distinct
```

Explanation: Folder.Files lists all files recursively, including files in sub folders. The filter excludes temporary Office lock files that start with a tilde. Csv.Document with Encoding 65001 reads UTF-8. The list of column names is computed from all files, so a column added in a later export does not break the query. The culture argument in TransformColumnTypes avoids wrong date parsing on a machine with a different regional setting. Table.Distinct removes rows that appear in overlapping exports.

## How to adapt
- Use a parameter: Home > Manage Parameters > New, and replace the FolderPath line with the parameter name, so colleagues can point the query to their own folder.
- SharePoint folder instead of local: replace the first step with SharePoint.Files("https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Reports", [ApiVersion = 15]) and filter on [Folder Path].
- Semicolon-separated files: change the Delimiter to ";".
- Load as connection only and merge it with other queries for lookups.

## Required permissions
Read access to the folder. For SharePoint folders, the account used in Data > Data source settings needs at least Read permission on the library. No Microsoft Graph permission is involved.

## Common mistakes
- Hard-coded column list in ExpandTableColumn: fails when a file lacks a column. The dynamic list above avoids that.
- Different header casing between files creates two columns.
- Leaving type detection on automatic: the first file decides, and later files can produce errors in some rows.
- Opening the workbook on another PC where the folder path does not exist; use a parameter or a SharePoint location.

## Performance and scaling notes
Power Query reads each file once per refresh. Hundreds of files of a few MB each refresh in seconds to minutes. Filter files by name or date as early as possible (for example on [Date modified]) so older files are never parsed. Disable background data previews when authoring very large folders.

title: Power Query M: flatten a Microsoft Graph JSON export with nested signInActivity
summary: Load a saved Graph users JSON response into Excel, expand nested records and lists, and convert ISO timestamps into proper date-time values.
body:
## What it does
Responses from Microsoft Graph are JSON with nested objects such as signInActivity and lists such as businessPhones. This script loads a JSON file saved from Graph Explorer, a script or a tool, expands the nested parts into columns, and turns ISO 8601 text into real dates for filtering and charts.

## Sample data layout
A file users.json with the structure Graph returns:

```
{
  "value": [
    {
      "id": "[user-object-id]",
      "displayName": "Anna Meyer",
      "userPrincipalName": "anna@contoso.example",
      "accountEnabled": true,
      "businessPhones": ["+49 711 000000"],
      "signInActivity": {
        "lastSignInDateTime": "2026-11-18T08:12:00Z",
        "lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime": "2026-11-19T02:00:00Z"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## The M script
Data > Get Data > From Other Sources > Blank Query > Advanced Editor:

```
let
  FilePath = "C:\Exports\users.json",
  Raw      = Json.Document(File.Contents(FilePath)),
  Items    = Raw[value],
  AsTable  = Table.FromList(Items, Splitter.SplitByNothing(), {"Record"}, null, ExtraValues.Error),
  Expanded = Table.ExpandRecordColumn(AsTable, "Record",
               {"id", "displayName", "userPrincipalName", "accountEnabled", "businessPhones", "signInActivity"}),
  Phones   = Table.TransformColumns(Expanded, {{"businessPhones",
               each if _ = null or List.IsEmpty(_) then null else Text.Combine(List.Transform(_, Text.From), "; "), type text}}),
  Activity = Table.ExpandRecordColumn(Phones, "signInActivity",
               {"lastSignInDateTime", "lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime"},
               {"LastSignIn", "LastNonInteractiveSignIn"}),
  Typed    = Table.TransformColumns(Activity, {
               {"LastSignIn", each if _ = null or _ = "" then null else DateTimeZone.FromText(_), type datetimezone},
               {"LastNonInteractiveSignIn", each if _ = null or _ = "" then null else DateTimeZone.FromText(_), type datetimezone},
               {"accountEnabled", each _, type logical}})
in
  Typed
```

Notes: ExpandRecordColumn takes the field names explicitly, so list only the properties you selected in the Graph query. The phone numbers are a JSON array and become a List value; the transformation joins them into one text cell. Users without sign-in data may have signInActivity set to null, and Table.ExpandRecordColumn handles null cells by returning nulls in the new columns. Graph can return 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z instead of null for accounts that never signed in; add a step that replaces dates earlier than 2000 with null if you prefer blanks.

## How to adapt
- Several pages: save each page and use Folder.Files plus the combine pattern, or store the pages as one array.
- Convert the time zone: DateTimeZone.SwitchZone(value, 1) for a fixed UTC+1 offset (no daylight saving time), then DateTimeZone.RemoveZone to get a plain datetime.
- Different resources (groups, devices): change the field list in ExpandRecordColumn; the pattern is the same.
- Live data from Graph requires an authenticated connector; the Web connector with anonymous authentication cannot supply a token safely, so prefer a scheduled export (for example from PowerShell) written to SharePoint or a folder.

## Required permissions
Excel needs read access to the JSON file only. To produce the file, the Graph call needs User.Read.All, and AuditLog.Read.All for signInActivity, plus Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.

## Common mistakes
- Pasting access tokens into M code to call Graph directly: tokens expire within an hour and are a security risk. Never store them in a workbook.
- Expanding a field that does not exist in every record without a default: the whole expansion fails. Use Record.FieldOrDefault inside a custom column for optional fields.
- Treating the timestamp as local time: the trailing Z means UTC.

## Performance and scaling notes
Json.Document loads the whole file in memory. Files of 50 to 100 MB are acceptable, larger ones should be split at the source or filtered with $select and $filter in the Graph request. Keep only the columns you need to reduce refresh time.

title: Forecast SharePoint storage growth with TREND and SEQUENCE and find the month a quota is exceeded
summary: Project the next twelve months of tenant or site storage use from monthly history and show the first month that exceeds the quota.
body:
## What it does
Admins often export storage used per month from the SharePoint admin center or from usage reports and need to know when the tenant or a site will hit its quota. These formulas fit a linear trend to the history, project the next twelve months, flag months over quota, and report the first month the quota is exceeded.

## Sample data layout
Table Storage with one row per month (first day of the month) and a named cell Quota holding the limit in GB:

| Month | UsedGB |
| 2026-01-01 | 812.4 |
| 2026-02-01 | 835.0 |
| 2026-03-01 | 861.9 |

Use at least six data points. Quota is a named cell, for example 1200. SEQUENCE, LET and TREND work in Excel 2021 and later; VSTACK and HSTACK need Microsoft 365 or Excel 2024.

## Formula 1: twelve-month forecast
```
=LET(
  h,  Storage[Month],
  y,  Storage[UsedGB],
  nd, DATE(YEAR(MAX(h)), MONTH(MAX(h)) + SEQUENCE(12), 1),
  fc, ROUND(TREND(y, h, nd), 1),
  VSTACK({"Month","Forecast GB","Over quota?"},
         HSTACK(nd, fc, IF(fc > Quota, "Yes", "No")))
)
```

DATE accepts the array produced by SEQUENCE, so the twelve future first-of-month dates are created in one step. TREND fits a straight line through the history and evaluates it at the new dates. Format the first column as mmm yyyy.

## Formula 2: first month over quota
```
=LET(
  h,  Storage[Month],
  y,  Storage[UsedGB],
  nd, DATE(YEAR(MAX(h)), MONTH(MAX(h)) + SEQUENCE(36), 1),
  fc, TREND(y, h, nd),
  XLOOKUP(TRUE, fc > Quota, nd, "Not within 36 months")
)
```
The result is a date serial, so format the cell as mmm yyyy.

## Formula 3: average monthly growth
```
=ROUND(SLOPE(Storage[UsedGB], Storage[Month]) * 30.4375, 1)
```
The slope is GB per day, multiplied by the average days per month.

## How to adapt
- Exponential growth: replace TREND with GROWTH(y, h, nd) when growth is percentage-based, for example because of Copilot-driven content creation or migrations.
- Per site: add a Site column and wrap the logic in a LAMBDA that takes a site name and uses FILTER on the table; call it with MAP over UNIQUE(Storage[Site]) (this works for Formula 2, which returns a single date per site, because MAP lambdas must return one value).
- Plan a purchase threshold: compare against 90 percent of Quota to get a warning date.
- Chart: select the forecast spill and Insert > Line Chart; to make the chart follow the size of the spill, define a name that refers to the spill range with the # operator (for example =Sheet1!$F$3#) and use that name as the series source.

## Required permissions
None in Excel. The history comes from SharePoint admin center usage data or reports; viewing it requires the SharePoint Administrator or Global Reader role, and Reports Reader for usage reports.

## Common mistakes
- Treating one-off migrations as trend: exclude outlier months or fit only the period after the migration.
- Using text months such as "Nov 2026": TREND needs real dates or numbers.
- Mixing GB and TB between months.
- Forgetting that recycle bin and version history count toward storage; a trend of content size alone underestimates consumption.

## Performance and scaling notes
These formulas operate on tens of rows and are instant. The main risk is not speed but model quality: a linear fit on twelve points is a rough guide. Re-check the forecast each month and keep the dated snapshots rather than overwriting history.

title: Advanced user queries in Microsoft Graph: filter, search, count and stale sign-ins
summary: Ready-to-run requests for listing users with $filter, $select, $orderby, $count and $search, plus the signInActivity query for inactive accounts.
body:
## What it does
These requests cover the user queries admins need daily: enabled member accounts sorted by name, a count, a name search, guest users, and accounts that have not signed in since a given date. Several of them are advanced queries and need the ConsistencyLevel header.

## Requests

Enabled members, sorted, with total count (advanced query because $orderby is combined with $filter):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=accountEnabled eq true and userType eq 'Member'&$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName,department,jobTitle,createdDateTime&$orderby=displayName&$count=true&$top=100
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Count only:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/$count
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Search by display name or mail:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$search="displayName:meyer" OR "mail:meyer"&$select=id,displayName,mail&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Guest users (userType is the simplest and most robust filter):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=userType eq 'Guest'&$select=id,displayName,mail,createdDateTime,externalUserState&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Alternative through the guest UPN suffix. endsWith is only supported as an advanced query, and the # must be encoded as %23:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=endsWith(userPrincipalName,'%23EXT%23@contoso.onmicrosoft.com')&$select=id,displayName,mail,createdDateTime&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Disabled accounts:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=accountEnabled eq false&$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Accounts without a sign-in since a date (needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2). Per the documentation, a filter on signInActivity cannot be combined with other filterable properties, and the page size is limited to 500 when signInActivity is selected or filtered:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$filter=signInActivity/lastSignInDateTime le 2026-08-20T00:00:00Z&$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName,accountEnabled,signInActivity&$top=500
```

## Response shape
```json
{
  "@odata.context": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/$metadata#users(...)",
  "@odata.count": 1842,
  "@odata.nextLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$skiptoken=[token]",
  "value": [ { "id": "[object-id]", "displayName": "Anna Meyer" } ]
}
```
Follow @odata.nextLink until it is absent. Do not use $skip: the documentation states that $skip is not supported on the users list.

## How to adapt
- More attributes: extend $select; only the default set is returned without it.
- Licensed users: $filter=assignedLicenses/any(u:u/skuId eq [sku-guid]) with $count=true and ConsistencyLevel: eventual (test it in Graph Explorer first).
- Users without any license: $filter=assignedLicenses/$count eq 0&$count=true with ConsistencyLevel: eventual.
- Export to a spreadsheet: pipe the value array into your tool of choice, or use the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK with the same filter.

## Required permissions
- Users list: delegated User.ReadBasic.All (limited properties), User.Read.All; application User.Read.All.
- signInActivity: additionally AuditLog.Read.All, and the signed-in admin needs a role such as Reports Reader, Security Reader or Global Reader for delegated access.
- Guest users have restricted directory access by default and usually cannot list other users. Always request the least privileged permission that returns the properties you need.

## Common mistakes
- Omitting ConsistencyLevel: eventual together with $count=true on advanced queries leads to a 400 error such as "Request_UnsupportedQuery".
- Not encoding # in guest UPNs.
- Expecting $top above 999 (or above 500 with signInActivity) to be honoured; you get capped pages.
- Combining signInActivity filter with other filters, which is not supported.
- Using $skip for paging instead of nextLink.

## Performance and throttling notes
Always use $select; it reduces payload and latency. Advanced queries rely on an eventually consistent index, so a user created seconds ago may not appear yet. Identity and access requests are throttled per tenant and app; on HTTP 429 wait for the Retry-After header value before retrying, and avoid parallelising more than a few paging loops.

title: Entra sign-in log queries with $filter: failed sign-ins, Conditional Access blocks and per-user checks
summary: Practical /auditLogs/signIns requests for time windows, failures by error code, Conditional Access failures and per-user investigations, with paging advice.
body:
## What it does
The sign-in log is the first stop for lockouts, MFA problems and suspicious access. These requests return the events you actually need instead of the whole log. Results come back newest first, so you rarely need $orderby.

## Requests

All sign-ins in a time window (always limit the time range to avoid timeouts):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z and createdDateTime le 2026-11-19T23:59:59Z&$top=500
```

Failed sign-ins for one user:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=userPrincipalName eq 'anna@contoso.example' and status/errorCode ne 0 and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-12T00:00:00Z&$top=100
```

Invalid username or password (error code 50126) in the last day:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=status/errorCode eq 50126 and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=200
```

Sign-ins blocked or failed by Conditional Access:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=conditionalAccessStatus eq 'failure' and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=200
```

Sign-ins to a particular application by name:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=startsWith(appDisplayName,'Microsoft Teams') and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=100
```

Interactive sign-ins only:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=isInteractive eq true and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=200
```

## Useful fields in the response
userPrincipalName, appDisplayName, ipAddress, clientAppUsed, createdDateTime, conditionalAccessStatus, status/errorCode, status/failureReason, deviceDetail/operatingSystem, location/countryOrRegion, riskLevelDuringSignIn. Common error codes: 50126 (bad credentials), 50053 (account locked), 50074 (MFA required), 53003 (blocked by Conditional Access), 50057 (account disabled).

Paging: each response contains @odata.nextLink while more data exists. Follow the complete link; it contains the skiptoken.

## How to adapt
- Replace the date placeholders with the window you need, always in UTC with a trailing Z.
- For a SIEM-style daily export, run the first request for the previous day at 01:00 UTC and store the page tokens only until the run finishes.
- Add $select=id,createdDateTime,userPrincipalName,appDisplayName,ipAddress,status to cut payload size. Be aware that appliedConditionalAccessPolicies is large; request it only when you need it.

## Required permissions
- Delegated and application: AuditLog.Read.All.
- Delegated access additionally requires a Microsoft Entra role such as Reports Reader, Security Reader, Security Operator, Security Administrator or Global Reader.
- The appliedConditionalAccessPolicies property is only included if the caller can also read Conditional Access data (for example the Policy.Read.ConditionalAccess application permission, or roles such as Conditional Access Administrator or Security Reader).

## Common mistakes
- Querying without a time filter: the call may time out because the log is large.
- Using local time instead of UTC in the filter.
- Expecting more history than your license provides; retention depends on the Microsoft Entra ID license (free tenants keep a short window; P1 and P2 keep longer).
- Assuming this endpoint returns every kind of sign-in. The v1.0 documentation says interactive sign-ins and successful federated sign-ins are included; non-interactive, service principal and managed identity sign-ins are reported separately in the portal and are not covered by these requests.
- Relying on a filter property that the documentation does not list. Only createdDateTime and appDisplayName are shown in the official examples; filters such as userPrincipalName, status/errorCode, conditionalAccessStatus and isInteractive are widely used but you should test them in Graph Explorer, and compare the result with the portal because unsupported query parameters can fail silently.

## Performance and throttling notes
$top is limited to 1000. Large exports are better done in daily windows than in one huge request. The sign-in endpoint has its own throttling limits; respect Retry-After on 429 responses and use exponential back-off. For continuous analysis, stream the logs to Log Analytics or a storage account with diagnostic settings instead of polling the API.

title: Track user changes with the Microsoft Graph users delta query and paging
summary: How to run the initial users delta sync, follow nextLink and deltaLink, and process changes and deletions on later runs without re-reading the directory.
body:
## What it does
Delta query returns only what changed since your last call, which is ideal for keeping an HR system, a database or a search index in sync with Microsoft Entra ID. The first run enumerates all users; later runs return created, updated and deleted users only.

## Step 1: initial synchronisation
Send a delta request with all query parameters you need. Other parameters can only be set on this first request; Graph encodes them into the tokens.
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$select=displayName,userPrincipalName,accountEnabled,department,jobTitle
Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=200
```

The response contains a page of users and an @odata.nextLink:
```json
{
  "@odata.nextLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$skiptoken=[skiptoken]",
  "value": [ { "id": "[object-id]", "displayName": "Anna Meyer", "userPrincipalName": "anna@contoso.example" } ]
}
```

## Step 2: follow the pages
Call the complete @odata.nextLink URL unchanged until the response contains @odata.deltaLink instead.
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$skiptoken=[skiptoken]
```
The last page returns:
```json
{
  "@odata.deltaLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$deltatoken=[deltatoken]",
  "value": []
}
```
Store the deltaLink securely (it is a pointer into tenant data) and discard the nextLinks.

## Step 3: incremental runs
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$deltatoken=[deltatoken]
```
Handle each item in value:
- A normal object with changed properties: create or update the record by id.
- An object containing "@removed": {"reason": "deleted"}: delete or deactivate the record.
Then continue until the new @odata.deltaLink appears and store it, replacing the old one.

## Only changed properties
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$deltatoken=[deltatoken]
Prefer: return=minimal
```
With return=minimal the response contains only the properties that changed. A property set to null is still included, so you can detect clearing a value.

## Track specific users only
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/delta?$filter=id eq '[object-id-1]' or id eq '[object-id-2]'
```
The only supported filter on this endpoint is on id, with a maximum of 50 objects.

## How to adapt
- Groups, applications, directory roles and many other directory resources have delta functions with the same pattern (for example /groups/delta).
- Store the deltaLink per sync job; running two consumers against one stored link causes missed changes.
- Schedule the job every 5 to 30 minutes; there is no value in polling faster than your data changes.

## Required permissions
Delegated: User.Read.All (higher privileged options include Directory.Read.All). Application: User.Read.All. Personal Microsoft accounts are not supported. Reading sensitive properties may require additional permissions.

## Common mistakes
- Changing $select between runs: query parameters live in the token; start a new sync instead.
- Keeping the nextLink as the checkpoint: only the deltaLink is the checkpoint.
- Not handling @removed objects, so deleted accounts stay in the target system.
- Expecting licenseAssignmentStates changes to appear; they are not tracked by user delta.
- Assuming the order of changes: use the last occurrence of an id if it appears twice.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use the Prefer: odata.maxpagesize header to control page size, and a narrow $select to keep responses small. If a deltaLink expires (the service returns an error such as 410 Gone, or a sync state not found message) start again with a full enumeration and reconcile. On HTTP 429 wait for Retry-After before the next page.

title: Microsoft Graph JSON batching: combine up to 20 requests with dependsOn and ConsistencyLevel
summary: A complete $batch example with parallel and dependent requests, per-request headers, error handling and the limits that matter in production.

title: Microsoft 365 groups in Graph: inventory with owners, ownerless groups and transitive members
summary: Requests to list Microsoft 365 and Teams-enabled groups, expand owners, find groups without owners or members, and read nested membership.
body:
## What it does
Group sprawl is a governance problem: groups without owners, empty groups, and groups whose membership is hidden in nested groups. These requests inventory groups and answer these questions. Note that advanced queries cannot be combined with $expand, so owners are retrieved in one request and ownerless groups in another.

## Requests

Microsoft 365 groups with creation date and owners:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=groupTypes/any(c:c eq 'Unified')&$select=id,displayName,mail,visibility,createdDateTime,resourceProvisioningOptions&$expand=owners($select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName)&$top=100
```

Groups that are Teams-enabled:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=resourceProvisioningOptions/Any(x:x eq 'Team')&$select=id,displayName,visibility
```

Groups without owners (advanced query, no $expand):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=owners/$count eq 0&$count=true&$select=id,displayName,createdDateTime
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Groups without members:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=members/$count eq 0&$count=true&$select=id,displayName,createdDateTime
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Dynamic membership groups:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=groupTypes/any(c:c eq 'DynamicMembership')&$select=id,displayName,membershipRule,membershipRuleProcessingState
```

Direct members (users only) with count:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/[group-id]/members/microsoft.graph.user?$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName&$count=true&$top=100
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Members including nested groups (transitive):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/[group-id]/transitiveMembers/microsoft.graph.user?$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName&$count=true
ConsistencyLevel: eventual
```

Owners of one group:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/[group-id]/owners?$select=id,displayName,userPrincipalName
```

## How to adapt
- Stale groups: combine the inventory with the Microsoft 365 group activity report (/reports/getOffice365GroupsActivityDetail(period='D90')) to find groups with no recent activity.
- Fix an ownerless group: POST /groups/[group-id]/owners/$ref with body {"@odata.id": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/[user-id]"}.
- Security groups only: $filter=securityEnabled eq true and mailEnabled eq false.

## Required permissions
- Reading groups, owners and members: delegated Group.Read.All or GroupMember.Read.All (for membership only); application Group.Read.All or GroupMember.Read.All. Directory.Read.All also works but is broader.
- Adding an owner: Group.ReadWrite.All (or Directory.ReadWrite.All), and an appropriate role such as Groups Administrator for delegated calls.
- Reports: Reports.Read.All.

## Common mistakes
- Adding $expand to an advanced query: it is not supported; use a second request.
- $expand=owners returns at most 20 items per group; query /owners if you need all.
- Forgetting the type cast microsoft.graph.user and getting groups and devices mixed in the members list.
- Missing ConsistencyLevel header or $count=true on count-based filters.
- Assuming members includes nested members; use transitiveMembers for that.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use $select, as groups have many properties. Expanding owners for 5,000 groups is cheaper than one call per group, but on large tenants use $top=100 or less with $expand. Directory throttling is per tenant; honour Retry-After. For regular inventories, run it weekly and store the result, rather than querying live every time.

title: SharePoint via Microsoft Graph: find a site, list its lists and filter list items on fields
summary: Requests to resolve a site by path, enumerate lists and libraries, and query list items with $expand=fields and $filter, including the indexed column caveat.
body:
## What it does
This sequence takes you from a SharePoint URL to the items in a list: resolve the site id, list the lists and document libraries, then read items with selected fields and a filter. It replaces many CSOM or REST scripts with plain Graph calls.

## Step 1: get the site
By path (hostname, colon, server-relative path):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/contoso.sharepoint.com:/sites/Marketing?$select=id,displayName,webUrl
```
By keyword search:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites?search=marketing&$select=id,displayName,webUrl
```
The id has the form hostname,site-collection-guid,web-guid. Use the complete value in later URLs.

## Step 2: lists and libraries
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists?$select=id,displayName,webUrl,list&$top=100
```
The list facet shows the template (for example genericList or documentLibrary) and whether the list is hidden. Document libraries also appear as drives:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/drives?$select=id,name,driveType,webUrl
```

## Step 3: columns
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/columns?$select=name,displayName,indexed,readOnly
```
Use the internal name (name) in $select and $filter, not the display name.

## Step 4: items with fields and a filter
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/items?$expand=fields($select=Title,Status,DueDate)&$filter=fields/Status eq 'Open'&$top=200
Prefer: HonorNonIndexedQueriesWarningMayFailRandomly
```
The Prefer header allows filtering on a column that is not indexed. Without it, Graph returns an error asking you to index the column. The header is described in Microsoft Q&A and community answers rather than on the listItem reference page, and its name is a warning: such queries can fail on large lists (over the list view threshold of 5,000 items), so index the column instead whenever you can.

Response:
```json
{
  "value": [
    { "id": "12", "webUrl": "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Marketing/Lists/Tasks/12_.000",
      "fields": { "Title": "Prepare campaign", "Status": "Open", "DueDate": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z" } }
  ],
  "@odata.nextLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/items?$skiptoken=[token]"
}
```

## Create an item
```http
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/items
Content-Type: application/json

{ "fields": { "Title": "New task", "Status": "Open" } }
```

## How to adapt
- Users in person columns appear as lookup ids (AuthorLookupId); resolve them separately.
- Filter by date: $filter=fields/DueDate lt '2026-12-31T00:00:00Z' on an indexed column.
- Change tracking: GET /sites/[site-id]/lists/[list-id]/items/delta for incremental reads.

## Required permissions
- Read sites, lists and items: delegated Sites.Read.All; application Sites.Read.All.
- Create or update items: Sites.ReadWrite.All.
- For application access limited to chosen sites, use Sites.Selected and grant the app per site through the site permissions endpoint; this is the recommended least privilege for production apps.

## Common mistakes
- Using the display name of a column instead of its internal name (for example Due_x0020_Date).
- Filtering on several indexed columns at once; only one indexed field can be filtered at a time.
- Forgetting $expand=fields: items then only contain metadata, not your column values.
- Truncating the site id; use the whole three-part value.
- Granting Sites.Read.All to an automation that only needs one site.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use $select inside fields to cut payload. Page with @odata.nextLink; $top up to 200 is typical for list items. SharePoint throttles by resource units and returns 429 or 503 with Retry-After; always honour it, and send a descriptive User-Agent for app traffic as recommended in the SharePoint throttling guidance.

title: OneDrive and SharePoint library change tracking with drive delta and downloadUrl
summary: Use the drive delta function for an initial sync and incremental changes, handle deleted items, and download file content without extra permission lookups.
body:
## What it does
Delta query on a drive returns files and folders that were added, changed or deleted since your last call. It is the right tool for backup jobs, search indexers and compliance exports that must not rescan millions of files every night. It works for OneDrive and for SharePoint document libraries.

## Choose the drive
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/drive?$select=id,driveType,webUrl
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/[site-id]/drives?$select=id,name,webUrl
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/[user-id]/drive?$select=id,webUrl
```

## Initial enumeration
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/root/delta?$select=id,name,size,lastModifiedDateTime,file,folder,deleted,parentReference&$top=200
```
Follow @odata.nextLink until the response contains @odata.deltaLink. Store the deltaLink.

```json
{
  "value": [
    { "id": "[item-id]", "name": "Budget.xlsx", "size": 48213, "lastModifiedDateTime": "2026-11-18T09:12:44Z",
      "file": { "mimeType": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet" },
      "parentReference": { "driveId": "[drive-id]", "id": "[parent-id]" } },
    { "id": "[other-item-id]", "name": "old.txt", "deleted": {} }
  ],
  "@odata.deltaLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/root/delta?token=[token]"
}
```

## Incremental run
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/root/delta?token=[token]
```
Apply each item by id. Items with the deleted facet must be removed from your index. The same item can appear more than once; use the last occurrence. parentReference.path is not populated in delta results, so track the hierarchy by ids.

## Start from now (skip history)
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/root/delta?token=latest
```
This returns an empty value array and a deltaLink for future changes.

## Download content
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/[drive-id]/items/[item-id]/content
```
The response is a redirect (302) to a short-lived pre-authenticated URL. Alternatively request it in the metadata: $select=id,name,@microsoft.graph.downloadUrl. Do not store download URLs; they expire after a short time and must not be shared.

## Resync handling
If the service cannot return changes for your token, it responds with 410 Gone and a Location header for a fresh enumeration. After the enumeration, reconcile with your local state (the error code resyncChangesApplyDifferences or resyncChangesUploadDifferences tells you how).

## How to adapt
- Sharing changes: add the headers Prefer: deltashowremovedasdeleted, deltatraversepermissiongaps, deltashowsharingchanges to get sharing-change annotations; permission scanning scenarios require the Sites.FullControl.All application permission.
- A single folder is not a documented delta scope; run delta on the root and filter by parent ids on your side.
- Large files: a simple upload (PUT .../content) supports files up to 250 MB; above that, or for resumable uploads, use createUploadSession.

## Required permissions
Delegated: Files.Read (least privileged for own drive), Files.Read.All for other drives; Sites.Read.All also works for SharePoint libraries. Application: Files.Read.All (or Sites.Read.All). Application access to all files is highly sensitive; prefer Sites.Selected where the scenario allows it.

## Common mistakes
- Trying to rebuild paths from parentReference.path in delta results.
- Treating deltaLink as permanent: protect it like a credential, and handle 410.
- Deleting a folder locally before its children are processed; delete folders only when empty.
- Logging download URLs.
- Starting a new full enumeration every night instead of using the stored deltaLink.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use $select to avoid large payloads and $top for page size. SharePoint and OneDrive throttle by resource units; delta calls are cheaper than recursive children listing. On 429 or 503, respect Retry-After, and schedule heavy initial enumerations outside business hours.

title: Mailbox triage with Microsoft Graph: unread filter, $select, move and mark as read
summary: Requests for reading unread inbox messages efficiently, searching, moving messages to folders, marking them read, and tracking changes with message delta.
body:
## What it does
Build a lightweight triage tool or automation: list unread messages from the last day, pull only the fields you need, move processed messages to a folder, and track new arrivals with delta. All requests use the signed-in mailbox (/me) and can be switched to /users/[id] for application access.

## Requests

Unread messages from a given time, newest first (properties in $orderby must also appear in $filter):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/mailFolders/inbox/messages?$filter=isRead eq false and receivedDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$orderby=receivedDateTime desc&$select=id,subject,from,receivedDateTime,hasAttachments,importance,webLink&$top=25
```

Text body instead of HTML (smaller, easier to process):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages/[message-id]?$select=subject,body,from
Prefer: outlook.body-content-type="text"
```

Search (cannot be combined with $filter or $orderby):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages?$search="from:anna AND subject:budget"&$select=id,subject,from,receivedDateTime&$top=25
```

Messages with attachments from a sender:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages?$filter=from/emailAddress/address eq 'anna@contoso.example' and hasAttachments eq true&$select=id,subject,receivedDateTime
```

List folders to get the target folder id:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/mailFolders?$select=id,displayName,totalItemCount,unreadItemCount&$top=50
```

Mark as read:
```http
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages/[message-id]
Content-Type: application/json

{ "isRead": true }
```

Move to a folder (a well-known name such as archive also works as destinationId):
```http
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages/[message-id]/move
Content-Type: application/json

{ "destinationId": "[folder-id]" }
```
The move returns a new message with a new id, so store the returned id if you need to reference it later.

Incremental changes in the inbox:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/mailFolders/inbox/messages/delta?$select=subject,from,receivedDateTime,isRead
Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=50
```
Follow @odata.nextLink until @odata.deltaLink, store it, and call it on the next run.

## How to adapt
- Application access to a shared mailbox: replace /me with /users/[mailbox-id-or-upn] and limit the app with an application access policy in Exchange Online, so it cannot read every mailbox.
- Stable ids across moves: add Prefer: IdType="ImmutableId".
- Categorise instead of move: PATCH with {"categories": ["Processed"]}.

## Required permissions
- Read: delegated Mail.Read (Mail.ReadBasic for limited fields); application Mail.Read.
- Mark as read, move, categorise: Mail.ReadWrite.
- Send mail would need Mail.Send; keep triage tools read/write only.
- Application permissions grant access to all mailboxes unless restricted by an application access policy or role-based access control for applications in Exchange Online.

## Common mistakes
- Combining $search with $filter or $orderby: not supported.
- Ordering by a property that is not in the filter: the request fails with an InefficientFilter error.
- Reading full HTML bodies for thousands of messages when only metadata is needed.
- Reusing the original id after a move.
- Granting tenant-wide Mail.ReadWrite to a simple automation.

## Performance and throttling notes
Outlook resources allow a limited number of concurrent requests per app and mailbox (commonly four), and 429 responses carry Retry-After. Use $select, $top up to 50 for bodies and larger for metadata, and delta instead of repeated full scans. Batch several reads with $batch, but keep concurrency modest.

title: Security alerts_v2 and incidents in Microsoft Graph: filter, triage and update alerts
summary: Requests to list alerts by severity, status and source, read incidents with alerts, and update status, classification and assignment of an alert.
body:
## What it does
The unified Microsoft Graph security API exposes alerts and incidents from Microsoft Defender XDR products and other sources in one place. These requests let a script or SOC dashboard pull high-severity new alerts, see them grouped as incidents, and update their state. Use alerts_v2 and incidents; the older legacy alerts endpoint is deprecated.

## Requests

New high-severity alerts (alerts_v2 documents $filter, $top, $skip and $count; it does not document $orderby, and recent alerts are returned first):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2?$filter=severity eq 'high' and status eq 'new'&$top=100
```

Alerts from one product created after a date:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2?$filter=serviceSource eq 'microsoftDefenderForEndpoint' and createdDateTime ge 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z&$top=100
```

Alerts assigned to an analyst:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2?$filter=assignedTo eq 'analyst@contoso.example'
```

One alert with its details and evidence:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2/[alert-id]
```

Active incidents with their alerts:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/incidents?$filter=status eq 'active'&$expand=alerts&$top=25
```

## Update an alert
```http
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2/[alert-id]
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "status": "inProgress",
  "assignedTo": "analyst@contoso.example",
  "classification": "truePositive",
  "determination": "malware"
}
```
Valid status values are new, inProgress and resolved. Classification and determination use the enumerations documented for the alert resource (for example falsePositive, truePositive, informationalExpectedActivity). Set them when resolving an alert.

## Paging
Responses contain @odata.nextLink while more alerts remain. Follow it. You can also page with $top and $skip as in $top=100&$skip=200, but nextLink is more robust.

## How to adapt
- Daily digest: filter on createdDateTime for the last 24 hours and group by serviceSource and severity on the client.
- Only unresolved: status ne 'resolved' (check the filter support for ne on the property in the current documentation).
- Hand off to a ticket system: store alert id, incidentId, title, severity, and the alertWebUrl property so analysts can open the Defender portal directly.

## Required permissions
- Read alerts: SecurityAlert.Read.All (delegated and application).
- Update alerts: SecurityAlert.ReadWrite.All.
- Read incidents: SecurityIncident.Read.All; update incidents: SecurityIncident.ReadWrite.All.
- Delegated calls also need the signed-in user to hold a supported role, for example Security Reader, Global Reader, Security Operator or Security Administrator.

## Common mistakes
- Calling the deprecated /security/alerts endpoint in new code.
- Using $orderby or $expand=evidence on alerts_v2 and getting errors; they are not documented for that endpoint.
- Using filter properties that are not supported; filters work on assignedTo, classification, determination, createdDateTime, lastUpdateDateTime, severity, serviceSource and status.
- Forgetting that application permissions here expose all security data in the tenant; protect the app registration, use certificates, and restrict who can use it.
- Updating status without a classification when resolving.

## Performance and throttling notes
Security API calls are throttled per app and tenant; keep polling at a sensible interval (every few minutes is usually enough) and honour Retry-After. Prefer filters on createdDateTime or lastUpdateDateTime so each poll fetches only recent alerts, and store the timestamp of the last processed alert as your checkpoint.

title: Intune managed devices in Graph: find noncompliant Windows devices and trigger a sync
summary: Requests to list managed devices with $filter and $select, look at compliance and last sync time, and send a sync action to selected devices.
body:
## What it does
Use these requests to get a current view of device compliance without opening the Intune admin center: noncompliant Windows devices, devices that have not checked in for a while, and the details of one device. Then trigger a remote sync for a device so that it reports compliance again. Intune license is required in the tenant.

## Requests

Test first: the Microsoft Learn page for listing managedDevices shows no $filter examples and does not say which properties and operators are supported. The three filter requests below use properties that exist on the managedDevice resource (complianceState, operatingSystem, lastSyncDateTime, userPrincipalName), but filter support per property is not documented. Run each one in Graph Explorer first and compare the count with the Intune admin center, because unsupported query parameters can fail silently. If a filter misbehaves, drop it and filter on the client side after $select.

Noncompliant Windows devices (test first; complianceState values are lowercase: compliant, noncompliant, inGracePeriod, conflict, error, unknown, configManager):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?$filter=complianceState eq 'noncompliant' and operatingSystem eq 'Windows'&$select=id,deviceName,userPrincipalName,operatingSystem,osVersion,complianceState,lastSyncDateTime,managedDeviceOwnerType&$top=100
```

Devices that last synced before a date (test first):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?$filter=lastSyncDateTime le 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z&$select=id,deviceName,userPrincipalName,lastSyncDateTime,complianceState&$top=100
```

Devices of one user (test first):
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?$filter=userPrincipalName eq 'anna@contoso.example'&$select=id,deviceName,operatingSystem,complianceState
```

One device with full details:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices/[managed-device-id]
```

Compliance policy results for one device:
```http
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices/[managed-device-id]/deviceCompliancePolicyStates
```

Trigger a sync (no request body, returns 204 No Content):
```http
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices/[managed-device-id]/syncDevice
```

## Response example
```json
{
  "value": [
    {
      "id": "[managed-device-id]",
      "deviceName": "LT-ANNA-01",
      "userPrincipalName": "anna@contoso.example",
      "operatingSystem": "Windows",
      "osVersion": "10.0.26100.1000",
      "complianceState": "noncompliant",
      "lastSyncDateTime": "2026-11-18T07:41:09Z"
    }
  ],
  "@odata.nextLink": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/managedDevices?$skiptoken=[token]"
}
```

## How to adapt
- Not every property supports every operator in Intune endpoints. If a filter returns an error, test it in Graph Explorer, filter by another property, or filter on the client side after $select.
- Join to Microsoft Entra ID with the azureADDeviceId property to find the directory device object.
- Report on all platforms by dropping the operatingSystem filter, or use iOS, Android and macOS values.
- Devices in a grace period report inGracePeriod, not noncompliant, so the first request does not return them; query complianceState eq 'inGracePeriod' separately if you need them.
- Bulk sync: loop over the ids returned by the first request, with a delay between calls and the $batch endpoint (up to 20 sync requests per batch).

## Required permissions
- Reading managed devices: DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All (delegated and application).
- Sync and other remote actions: DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All (delegated and application). Do not use ReadWrite permissions for actions that require this one.
- Delegated calls also require an Intune role with the corresponding rights, for example Help Desk Operator or Intune Administrator through role-based access control.

## Common mistakes
- Trusting an undocumented $filter without testing it; managedDevices filters are not covered by the reference page.
- Sending a body with syncDevice; the request body must be empty.
- Using the Microsoft Entra device id instead of the Intune managed device id in the URL.
- Granting PrivilegedOperations.All to a reporting app that only needs Read.All.
- Treating lastSyncDateTime as the last user activity; it is the last check-in with Intune.
- Ignoring paging and only seeing the first 100 devices.

## Performance and throttling notes
Use $select to avoid the large default device object. Intune applies service-specific throttling; on 429 respond to Retry-After and keep sync loops slow (for example one call per second). Remote actions are queued, and the device syncs when it next contacts the service, so do not retry repeatedly. For very large estates, use Intune data exports or the reporting endpoints under /deviceManagement/reports for bulk data, rather than paging through every device.

title: Entra guest user report with stale invitations and last sign-in
summary: Microsoft Graph PowerShell script that exports every B2B guest with invitation state, age, last sign-in and optional group count, and flags stale invitations and inactive guests.
body:
# Entra guest user report with stale invitations and last sign-in

Guests accumulate quietly: project partners, vendors, one-off invitations. This script gives you a reviewable CSV of all guest accounts in Microsoft Entra ID, with the signals you need to decide who stays.

## What it does
- Reads all users with userType Guest through Microsoft Graph.
- Adds invitation state (PendingAcceptance or Accepted), account age, external domain and last sign-in.
- Optionally counts group memberships per guest (slower, one call per guest).
- Classifies each guest as Active, InactiveGuest or StaleInvitation based on a threshold you set.
- Exports a CSV and prints a per-domain summary.

## Script
```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Exports a report of Entra ID guest users.
.EXAMPLE
  .\Get-GuestReport.ps1 -StaleDays 120 -IncludeGroupCount
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]$OutputPath = ".\GuestUserReport_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd').csv",
    [ValidateRange(1,3650)]
    [int]$StaleDays = 90,
    [switch]$IncludeGroupCount
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# 1. Connect with read-only delegated scopes (no secrets in the script)
try {
    Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.Read.All','AuditLog.Read.All' -NoWelcome
}
catch {
    Write-Error "Connection to Microsoft Graph failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    return
}

# 2. Read all guests, selecting only the properties we need
$props = 'id','displayName','mail','userPrincipalName','companyName','createdDateTime',
         'externalUserState','externalUserStateChangeDateTime','accountEnabled','signInActivity'
try {
    $guests = Get-MgUser -Filter "userType eq 'Guest'" -All -Property $props -PageSize 500
}
catch {
    Write-Error "Could not read guest users: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    return
}
Write-Host "Found $($guests.Count) guest accounts." -ForegroundColor Cyan

$cutoff = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$StaleDays)
$report = foreach ($g in $guests) {
    $sa = $g.SignInActivity
    $lastSignIn = @($sa.LastSuccessfulSignInDateTime, $sa.LastSignInDateTime, $sa.LastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime) |
        Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Descending | Select-Object -First 1

    $groupCount = $null
    if ($IncludeGroupCount) {
        try { $groupCount = @(Get-MgUserMemberOf -UserId $g.Id -All -ErrorAction Stop).Count }
        catch { $groupCount = -1 }   # -1 = lookup failed
    }

    $status = 'Active'
    if ($g.ExternalUserState -eq 'PendingAcceptance' -and $g.CreatedDateTime -lt $cutoff) {
        $status = 'StaleInvitation'
    }
    elseif ($g.ExternalUserState -ne 'PendingAcceptance' -and (-not $lastSignIn -or $lastSignIn -lt $cutoff)) {
        $status = 'InactiveGuest'
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        DisplayName     = $g.DisplayName
        Mail            = $g.Mail
        Domain          = if ($g.Mail) { ($g.Mail -split '@')[-1] } else { '' }
        Company         = $g.CompanyName
        AccountEnabled  = $g.AccountEnabled
        InvitationState = $g.ExternalUserState
        Created         = $g.CreatedDateTime
        AgeDays         = [int]((Get-Date) - $g.CreatedDateTime).TotalDays
        LastSignIn      = $lastSignIn
        GroupCount      = $groupCount
        Status          = $status
        ObjectId        = $g.Id
    }
}

$report | Sort-Object Status, Domain | Export-Csv -Path $OutputPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "Report written to $OutputPath" -ForegroundColor Green

$report | Group-Object Status | Select-Object Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize
$report | Group-Object Domain | Sort-Object Count -Descending |
    Select-Object -First 10 Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize
```

## Required permissions/roles
- Delegated scopes: User.Read.All and AuditLog.Read.All (admin consent is needed once).
- Signed-in role: Global Reader, Reports Reader or Security Reader is enough for reading; no write role is required.
- signInActivity needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 in the tenant.

## How to adapt
- Remove guests after review: pipe approved ObjectIds into Remove-MgUser -UserId with -WhatIf first, or disable them with Update-MgUser -AccountEnabled:$false.
- Re-send invitations for pending guests with New-MgInvitation -InvitedUserEmailAddress -InviteRedirectUrl (scope User.Invite.All).
- Add a Team or group name column by expanding the memberOf results when you need a per-project view.
- Schedule it monthly in Azure Automation and mail the CSV to the guest sponsor or security team.

## Common mistakes
- Treating an empty last sign-in as proof of inactivity: sign-in data starts when the feature was enabled for the tenant, so combine it with account age.
- Forgetting that guests can hold access through group, Team or SharePoint sharing links, so disabling the account is safer than deleting during review.
- Running with -IncludeGroupCount on tens of thousands of guests without expecting throttling; run it off-hours.
- Reviewing only the UPN: guest UPNs contain #EXT#, so use the Mail column to see the real external address and domain.

title: Find inactive Microsoft 365 user accounts and disable them safely
summary: Report enabled Entra ID accounts with no sign-in for N days, skip break-glass and synced accounts, and optionally disable the rest with WhatIf and Confirm support.
body:
# Find inactive Microsoft 365 user accounts and disable them safely

Inactive but licensed accounts cost money and widen your attack surface. This script finds them using the signInActivity data in Microsoft Entra ID, writes a CSV for review, and can disable the confirmed ones.

## What it does
- Lists enabled accounts (members, optionally guests) with their last interactive, non-interactive and successful sign-in.
- Treats an account as inactive when its newest activity (or, for accounts that never signed in, its creation date) is older than the threshold.
- Counts assigned licenses so you can quantify savings.
- Skips excluded UPNs such as break-glass accounts and flags accounts synced from on-premises AD, which must be disabled there.
- With -DisableAccounts it disables the rest, honoring -WhatIf and -Confirm. The CSV is still written during a -WhatIf run, so you can review the candidates first.

## Script
```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Reports and optionally disables inactive Entra ID accounts.
.EXAMPLE
  .\Get-InactiveUsers.ps1 -InactiveDays 120 -ExcludeUpn 'breakglass1@contoso.com'
  .\Get-InactiveUsers.ps1 -InactiveDays 120 -DisableAccounts -WhatIf
#>
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess, ConfirmImpact = 'High')]
param(
    [ValidateRange(30,3650)][int]$InactiveDays = 90,
    [string[]]$ExcludeUpn = @(),
    [switch]$IncludeGuests,
    [switch]$DisableAccounts,
    [string]$OutputPath = ".\InactiveUsers_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd').csv"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$scopes = @('User.Read.All','AuditLog.Read.All')
if ($DisableAccounts) { $scopes = @('User.Read.All','User.EnableDisableAccount.All','AuditLog.Read.All') }

try { Connect-MgGraph -Scopes $scopes -NoWelcome }
catch { Write-Error "Graph connection failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

$props = 'id','displayName','userPrincipalName','userType','accountEnabled','createdDateTime',
         'assignedLicenses','onPremisesSyncEnabled','signInActivity','department','jobTitle'
$filter = "accountEnabled eq true"
if (-not $IncludeGuests) { $filter += " and userType eq 'Member'" }

try { $users = Get-MgUser -Filter $filter -All -Property $props -PageSize 500 }
catch { Write-Error "User query failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

$cutoff = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$InactiveDays)
$rows = foreach ($u in $users) {
    if ($ExcludeUpn -contains $u.UserPrincipalName) { continue }
    $sa = $u.SignInActivity
    $last = @($sa.LastSuccessfulSignInDateTime,$sa.LastSignInDateTime,$sa.LastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime) |
            Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    $reference = if ($last) { $last } else { $u.CreatedDateTime }
    if ($reference -ge $cutoff) { continue }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        UserPrincipalName = $u.UserPrincipalName
        DisplayName       = $u.DisplayName
        UserType          = $u.UserType
        Department        = $u.Department
        LastActivity      = $last
        NeverSignedIn     = -not $last
        DaysInactive      = [int]((Get-Date) - $reference).TotalDays
        LicenseCount      = @($u.AssignedLicenses).Count
        SyncedFromAD      = [bool]$u.OnPremisesSyncEnabled
        Action            = if ($u.OnPremisesSyncEnabled) { 'Disable in on-prem AD' } else { 'Disable in Entra' }
        ObjectId          = $u.Id
    }
}

# -WhatIf:$false keeps the report writing even during a -WhatIf run (the script's -WhatIf would otherwise be inherited by Export-Csv)
$rows | Sort-Object DaysInactive -Descending | Export-Csv $OutputPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8 -WhatIf:$false
Write-Host ("{0} inactive accounts, {1} licenses assigned. Report: {2}" -f `
    @($rows).Count, ($rows | Measure-Object LicenseCount -Sum).Sum, $OutputPath) -ForegroundColor Cyan

if ($DisableAccounts) {
    foreach ($r in $rows | Where-Object { -not $_.SyncedFromAD }) {
        if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($r.UserPrincipalName, "Disable account (inactive $($r.DaysInactive) days)")) {
            try { Update-MgUser -UserId $r.ObjectId -AccountEnabled:$false -ErrorAction Stop }
            catch { Write-Warning "Failed for $($r.UserPrincipalName): $($_.Exception.Message)" }
        }
    }
}
```

## Required permissions/roles
- Report only: User.Read.All and AuditLog.Read.All; Global Reader or Reports Reader.
- Disabling: User.EnableDisableAccount.All together with User.Read.All (User.ReadWrite.All also works but is broader); the signed-in admin needs User Administrator or higher. Disabling privileged accounts additionally requires Privileged Authentication Administrator or Global Administrator.
- signInActivity requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.

## How to adapt
- Add a license-removal step with Set-MgUserLicense -UserId -AddLicenses @() -RemoveLicenses @(skuId) after a grace period.
- Exclude service accounts by a naming convention or an extension attribute instead of a static list.
- Move disabled users into a review group, wait 30 days, then delete and rely on the recycle bin (30 days) as a safety net.
- Send the CSV to each manager using the Manager property (Get-MgUserManager) before disabling.
- The script uses ConfirmImpact High, so every account prompts. After you reviewed the -WhatIf output, add -Confirm:$false to run unattended.

## Common mistakes
- Disabling shared mailbox, room or service accounts that never sign in interactively. Exclude them first.
- Forgetting break-glass accounts. They are supposed to be inactive.
- Using only LastSignInDateTime: non-interactive sign-ins (mobile mail, token refresh) keep an account in use, so the script takes the newest of all three values.
- Running with -DisableAccounts before reviewing the CSV. Always do a -WhatIf pass first.

title: MFA registration and strength report for all Entra ID users
summary: Uses the authentication methods registration report to list who has no MFA, who relies on weak methods such as SMS, and which admins lack phishing-resistant methods.
body:
# MFA registration and strength report for all Entra ID users

Instead of querying authentication methods user by user (slow and heavily throttled), this script reads the tenant-wide registration report in one paged call and classifies each user by MFA strength.

## What it does
- Pulls userRegistrationDetails for every user with Get-MgReportAuthenticationMethodUserRegistrationDetail.
- Classifies users as NoMFA, WeakMFA (only SMS, voice or email style methods), StandardMFA (authenticator app or OTP) or PhishingResistant (passkey, FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business, certificate).
- Highlights administrators without phishing-resistant methods.
- Exports a CSV and prints a summary table you can paste into a security review.

## Script
```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  MFA registration and method-strength report.
.EXAMPLE
  .\Get-MfaReport.ps1 -AdminsOnly
  .\Get-MfaReport.ps1 -OnlyGaps -OutputPath C:\Temp\mfa-gaps.csv
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$AdminsOnly,
    [switch]$OnlyGaps,
    [string]$OutputPath = ".\MfaReport_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd').csv"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

try { Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'AuditLog.Read.All' -NoWelcome }
catch { Write-Error "Graph connection failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

try {
    $details = Get-MgReportAuthenticationMethodUserRegistrationDetail -All -PageSize 500
}
catch {
    Write-Error "Registration report failed. Check license (Entra ID P1) and role. $($_.Exception.Message)"
    return
}

if ($AdminsOnly) { $details = $details | Where-Object { $_.IsAdmin } }

$phishingResistant = 'fido2|passKey|windowsHelloForBusiness|certificate'
$weakOnly          = '^(mobilePhone|alternateMobilePhone|officePhone|email|securityQuestion)$'

$report = foreach ($d in $details) {
    $methods = @($d.MethodsRegistered)
    $strength =
        if (-not $d.IsMfaRegistered)                                   { 'NoMFA' }
        elseif ($methods -match $phishingResistant)                    { 'PhishingResistant' }
        elseif (@($methods | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch $weakOnly }).Count -eq 0) { 'WeakMFA' }
        else                                                           { 'StandardMFA' }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        UserPrincipalName  = $d.UserPrincipalName
        DisplayName        = $d.UserDisplayName
        UserType           = $d.UserType
        IsAdmin            = $d.IsAdmin
        MfaRegistered      = $d.IsMfaRegistered
        MfaCapable         = $d.IsMfaCapable
        PasswordlessCapable= $d.IsPasswordlessCapable
        SsprRegistered     = $d.IsSsprRegistered
        Strength           = $strength
        Methods            = ($methods -join ';')
        LastUpdated        = $d.LastUpdatedDateTime
    }
}

if ($OnlyGaps) { $report = $report | Where-Object { $_.Strength -in 'NoMFA','WeakMFA' -or ($_.IsAdmin -and $_.Strength -ne 'PhishingResistant') } }

$report | Sort-Object IsAdmin -Descending | Export-Csv $OutputPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "Report written to $OutputPath" -ForegroundColor Green

$report | Group-Object Strength | Select-Object Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize
$report | Where-Object { $_.IsAdmin -and $_.Strength -ne 'PhishingResistant' } |
    Select-Object UserPrincipalName, Strength, Methods | Format-Table -AutoSize
```

## Required permissions/roles
- Delegated scope AuditLog.Read.All (admin consent required).
- Signed-in role: Reports Reader, Security Reader, Global Reader, Authentication Administrator or higher.
- The registration report requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 in the tenant.

## How to adapt
- For per-user details (device names, phone numbers masked) call Get-MgUserAuthenticationMethod -UserId and inspect the odata.type of each result; scope UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All.
- Feed the NoMFA list into a group and target it with a Conditional Access policy that requires registration or an authentication strength.
- Schedule weekly and track the NoMFA and WeakMFA counts as a security KPI.
- Filter by department or country using a join against Get-MgUser if you want regional breakdowns.

## Common mistakes
- Reading "MFA registered" as "MFA enforced". The report shows what users registered, not whether a policy requires it. Compare with Conditional Access sign-in results.
- Ignoring guests and service accounts: filter on UserType when the report is for employees only.
- Assuming SMS counts as strong. Treat it as the fallback you are trying to retire.
- Running per-user authentication method calls for 50,000 users instead of the registration report; you will hit throttling.

title: Intune device compliance export with per-policy failure details
summary: Exports all managed devices with compliance state, OS, last sync and encryption, flags stale devices, and lists devices failing each compliance policy using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
body:
# Intune device compliance export with per-policy failure details

Helpdesk and security teams keep asking "which devices are non-compliant and why?" This script produces two CSVs: a device inventory with compliance state, and a policy-level list of every device reporting NonCompliant, Error or Conflict.

## What it does
- Reads all Intune managed devices with Get-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice.
- Filters by operating system and compliance state on the client side (more reliable than combined server filters).
- Flags devices that have not synced for the number of days you choose.
- With -IncludePolicyStatus, loops through every device compliance policy and exports failing device statuses.
- Prints a summary by OS and compliance state.

## Script
```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Exports Intune device compliance data.
.EXAMPLE
  .\Export-IntuneCompliance.ps1 -OperatingSystem Windows -StaleDays 14 -IncludePolicyStatus
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [ValidateSet('All','Windows','iOS','Android','macOS')][string]$OperatingSystem = 'All',
    [switch]$NonCompliantOnly,
    [int]$StaleDays = 30,
    [switch]$IncludePolicyStatus,
    [string]$OutputFolder = '.'
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$scopes = @('DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All')
if ($IncludePolicyStatus) { $scopes += 'DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All' }

try { Connect-MgGraph -Scopes $scopes -NoWelcome }
catch { Write-Error "Graph connection failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

$props = 'id','deviceName','userPrincipalName','operatingSystem','osVersion','complianceState',
         'managedDeviceOwnerType','enrolledDateTime','lastSyncDateTime','manufacturer','model',
         'serialNumber','isEncrypted','azureADDeviceId','complianceGracePeriodExpirationDateTime'
try {
    $devices = Get-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice -All -PageSize 500 -Property $props
}
catch { Write-Error "Device query failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

if ($OperatingSystem -ne 'All') { $devices = $devices | Where-Object { $_.OperatingSystem -eq $OperatingSystem } }
if ($NonCompliantOnly)          { $devices = $devices | Where-Object { $_.ComplianceState -ne 'compliant' } }   # everything except 'compliant': includes noncompliant, inGracePeriod, error, conflict, unknown

$cutoff = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$StaleDays)
$deviceReport = foreach ($d in $devices) {
    [pscustomobject]@{
        DeviceName      = $d.DeviceName
        User            = $d.UserPrincipalName
        OS              = $d.OperatingSystem
        OSVersion       = $d.OsVersion
        Compliance      = $d.ComplianceState
        GraceExpires    = $d.ComplianceGracePeriodExpirationDateTime
        Ownership       = $d.ManagedDeviceOwnerType
        Encrypted       = $d.IsEncrypted
        Manufacturer    = $d.Manufacturer
        Model           = $d.Model
        Serial          = $d.SerialNumber
        Enrolled        = $d.EnrolledDateTime
        LastSync        = $d.LastSyncDateTime
        Stale           = ($d.LastSyncDateTime -lt $cutoff)
        EntraDeviceId   = $d.AzureADDeviceId
    }
}
$stamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd'
$devPath = Join-Path $OutputFolder "IntuneDevices_$stamp.csv"
$deviceReport | Export-Csv $devPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "Devices: $(@($deviceReport).Count) -> $devPath" -ForegroundColor Green
$deviceReport | Group-Object OS, Compliance | Select-Object Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize

if ($IncludePolicyStatus) {
    $failing = foreach ($p in Get-MgDeviceManagementDeviceCompliancePolicy -All) {
        try {
            $statuses = Get-MgDeviceManagementDeviceCompliancePolicyDeviceStatus -DeviceCompliancePolicyId $p.Id -All -ErrorAction Stop
        }
        catch { Write-Warning "Status failed for policy $($p.DisplayName): $($_.Exception.Message)"; continue }
        foreach ($s in $statuses | Where-Object { $_.Status -in 'nonCompliant','error','conflict' }) {
            [pscustomobject]@{
                Policy = $p.DisplayName; Device = $s.DeviceDisplayName; User = $s.UserPrincipalName
                Status = $s.Status; LastReported = $s.LastReportedDateTime
            }
        }
    }
    $polPath = Join-Path $OutputFolder "IntunePolicyFailures_$stamp.csv"
    $failing | Export-Csv $polPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
    $failing | Group-Object Policy, Status | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize
}
```

## Required permissions/roles
- DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All for devices; DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All for policy status.
- Roles: Intune Administrator, Global Reader, or an Intune custom role with read access to managed devices and compliance policies.

## How to adapt
- Trigger a sync for stale devices with Sync-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice -ManagedDeviceId (needs DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All); use -WhatIf awareness in your wrapper.
- Join with Entra device objects (Get-MgDevice) to find devices registered in Entra but missing in Intune.
- For detailed per-setting failures, query the compliance setting state summaries for a single policy.
- Send the policy failure CSV to the owning team and track the count weekly.

## Common mistakes
- Treating "inGracePeriod" as compliant. Grace periods expire and then Conditional Access blocks the user.
- Ignoring stale devices: a device that has not synced in months still shows its last known (often compliant) state.
- Running without paging on large tenants. Always use -All and a sensible -PageSize.
- Confusing Intune compliance state with Defender risk signals; they are separate inputs unless connected in a policy.
